lessons.title: Software Testing Fundamentals
lessons.concept: Software testing is the process of evaluating software to find defects and verify that it meets specified requirements. Testing helps reduce risk and improve quality, but it cannot prove the complete absence of bugs except in trivial cases.
lessons.formula: Goal: detect defects + verify behavior against requirements. Testing != proof of zero defects.
lessons.worked_example: Testing a login feature includes checking valid credentials, invalid passwords, empty fields, and lockout behavior to verify expected outcomes.
mistakes: Assuming passing tests means software is bug-free
Testing only happy paths and ignoring edge cases
Confusing testing with debugging (debugging finds/fixes cause after failure)
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Levels of Testing
lessons.concept: Common testing levels include unit testing (individual components), integration testing (interactions between components), system testing (end-to-end system behavior), and acceptance testing (validation against user/business needs).
lessons.formula: Typical progression: Unit -> Integration -> System -> Acceptance.
lessons.worked_example: Unit test verifies a function that calculates discount. Integration test verifies checkout module with payment service. System test verifies full purchase flow. Acceptance test confirms business requirements are met.
mistakes: Confusing unit and integration testing scopes
Skipping lower-level tests and relying only on system/UI tests
Assuming acceptance testing is only about technical correctness
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Test Types and Test Case Design
lessons.concept: Testing can be functional (what system does) or non-functional (performance, security, usability). Good test cases include clear inputs, steps, and expected results, and cover normal, boundary, and invalid scenarios.
lessons.formula: Test case elements: preconditions, input/steps, expected result, actual result. Cover equivalence classes and boundary values.
lessons.worked_example: For age input 18-60, boundary tests include 17, 18, 60, 61 along with typical valid values to check edges and normal behavior.
